markdown_content: ## Toon Shader (CLO 2026.0): Cartoon Rendering for 3D Window This section introduces **Toon Shader** as a new **CLO 2026.0** feature that makes avatars and garments look like cartoons, with controllable outline and color-shading behavior. It also clarifies where the effect is supported. In the **Property Editor**, open the **Materials** settings and locate **Materials Type**. Select **Toon** (the feature is referred to as *Toon Shader*). This option is described as working specifically with the **3D Window**. **Important limitation:** Toon Shader **only works with your 3D Window**. It **will not work with V-Ray** or when you are **rendering**. ## How to Enable Toon Shader in the Property Editor This section explains the exact workflow to apply Toon Shader via the **Materials Type** control in the **Property Editor**. 1. Open your **Closed Screen** (the 3D viewing interface is implied). 2. In the **Property Editor**, go to **Materials**. 3. Under **Materials Type**, choose **Toon**. After selecting Toon, the property editor reveals additional Toon Shader controls that affect the cartoon look. ## Toon Shader Controls: Color, Hardness/Softness, and Outlines This section covers the adjustable parameters Toon Shader exposes, including outline thickness/color and the hardness/softness of the cartoon shading. These controls determine how “toon” the avatar/garment appears. Once Toon is enabled, you can adjust: - **Color around** the model (overall look of the effect) - **Hardness vs. softness** (how sharp or smooth the toon shading appears) - **Color shifting** (how the coloring transitions across the surface) - **Outline styling**, including: - **Outline thickness** (e.g., thin vs. thick) - **Outline color** With these settings, you can create a **cartoonish-looking avatar and garments**, tuning the effect to match the desired style.
